2024 Edo Governorship Election Presidential Gubernatorial President Bola Tinubu met with Igbo stakeholders resident in Lagos at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts (National Theatre) in Lagos State on Monday, November 23, 2026. The town hall meeting, initiated under the platform of the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative, is spearheaded by the Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite, to mobilise support for President Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
President Bola Tinubu on Monday thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on 16 January 2027
He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians.
President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders and leaders of Ndigbo during a town hall meeting organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State.
He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous, and united Nigeria.
To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time.
“I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and God will continue to guide and bless our country. It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president.
“I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. Though tribes and tongues may differ, in brotherhood we stand. None of us told God when we were born where we would be born or what language we would speak. Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no control over yourself. God created you, created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians.

“Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house, geographically called Nigeria,” the president told the gathering.
The president said his administration recognises the significant contributions of the Igbo communities to Nigeria’s economic growth, assuring them that no section of the country would be left behind under the Renewed Hope Agenda.
President Tinubu appreciated the leadership of all the market leaders in Lagos for leaving their businesses to be at the gathering.
” To all of you, I am grateful for one thing: that you are here this afternoon. You left your businesses, left money-making to come and listen to the president, and I must say thank you,” he said.
The president expressed his determination to consolidate his administration’s economic gains.
He said national development requires collective commitment, mutual understanding, and cooperation, urging the Igbo community to embrace dialogue and constructive engagement to address challenges and advance their interests within the Nigerian federation.
President Tinubu told the gathering that all the South East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election. He mentioned Chidi Anyeagbu, owner of Chisco Motors; Dave Umahi, Doris Uzoka-Anite, and Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who were at the gathering, as people he has close connections with.
President Tinubu explained some of the reasons behind his policies, such as ensuring the tertiary schools are no longer paralysed by union strikes.
“To eliminate the crisis in the universities, to build good roads and the engineers that will maintain our cars, our children must be in school. Just because they are poor doesn’t mean they must not go to university or develop.
“We are doing that with NELFUND. The university is stable today because we are doing well. We are putting money in agriculture and trading, and anyone in the trade business can apply to the Bank of Industry and get a loan; anyone in agriculture can take a small farmers’ loan.
“We have to maintain this country for the sake of every one of us. The critical line in our national anthem is what I’m standing here for. I begged for it, and I am ready to serve.
“And I served the first term. The constitution says I can ask for a second term. I want a second term. As you are here today, you make me happy, you make me excited, and I will go home happy and eat (Akpu),” the president said.
President Tinubu also called on Ndigbo residents in Lagos to participate actively and vote for him, APC governorship candidate Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.
He commended the organisers of the town hall meeting for providing a platform for constructive engagement between the Federal Government and the Igbo community,
On his part, the host Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, rallied members of the Ndigbo to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, assuring the president of massive votes from the state in the 16 January 2027 presidential election.
Mr Sanwo-Olu described the turnout of Igbo leaders, traders, and business owners as proof that Lagos residents were united behind the president, despite the meeting being held on a Monday, when many participants had to leave their businesses to attend.
The governor urged the community to sustain the unity and support, saying Lagos would deliver an unprecedented number of votes for Tinubu.
He also praised Mr Tinubu as a detribalised Nigerian and nationalist, saying his administration had promoted development across the six geopolitical zones and strengthened national unity.
Mr Sanwo-Olu further commended the president for what he described as economic stability, increased investment and opportunities for young people, while thanking him for his contributions to Lagos State.
Describing the gathering as a reflection of the “One Lagos” spirit, the governor said the presence of people from different ethnic backgrounds demonstrated that residents could work together in support of a common political cause.
In her remarks, the Convener of the meeting and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite, declared the Igbo community’s commitment in Lagos State to supporting President Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the community has resolved to unite behind his leadership.
She said the Ndigbo had commenced grassroots mobilisation across Lagos State, with structures established at the polling-unit level ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
Also speaking, the former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, assured President Bola Tinubu of the Ndigbo’s support for his 2027 re-election bid, saying the gathering of Igbo leaders and stakeholders in Lagos demonstrated their unity and commitment to the president.
She said the community had recognised the importance of building political alliances with other geopolitical zones to achieve its future presidential ambition.
She assured the president that Ndigbo acknowledged the difficult circumstances under which his administration began and appreciated some of the government’s decisions.
She commended the president for removing the fuel subsidy, adding that the decision had improved sub-national fiscal capacity to meet salary obligations in their respective states.
The former minister also praised the administration for fulfilling its commitment to reviewing workers’ salaries every three years and introducing a national minimum wage of ₦70,000.
The leader of the Ndigbo Traders Association in Lagos, Tony Nwakeze, pledged members’ support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, while appealing for access to loans at a 5 per cent interest rate to help traders transition from importation to local manufacturing.
Mr Nwakeze said traders from Alaba, Trade Fair and Ladipo markets were seeking financial support to empower young people and expand their businesses.
He also assured the president that traders were prepared to organise themselves and adopt a cross-guarantee arrangement to ensure repayment of any loans granted to their members.
He also pledged that the market leadership would honour agreements reached with the government, stressing that traders had learnt from previous misunderstandings and were committed to sustaining a cordial relationship with the Lagos State Government.
He thanked the president for attending the meeting and promised that traders across Lagos markets would support him and honour every agreement reached with the government.
“We, the market people, will stand with you, support you and honour every agreement we enter into today,” he said.
